# dlasq1

> Computes all the singular values of a real upper bidiagonal matrix of.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlasq1 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlasq1';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlasq1( N, d, strideD, e, strideE, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows and columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | `d` stride length |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | `e` stride length |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 4 * N</sub> | **out** · Input array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of rows and columns in the matrix. $N \ge 0$.
- `d`: On entry, D contains the diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix whose SVD is desired. On normal exit, D contains the singular values in decreasing order.
- `e`: On entry, elements `E(1:N-1)` contain the off-diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix whose SVD is desired. On exit, E is overwritten.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlasq1.ndarray(
    N,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows and columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix, length N |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Off-diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix in `e[0..N-2]`, length N (overwritten on exit) |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `e` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 4 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array of length at least 4\*N |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of rows and columns in the matrix. $N \ge 0$.
- `d`: On entry, D contains the diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix whose SVD is desired. On normal exit, D contains the singular values in decreasing order.
- `e`: On entry, elements `E(1:N-1)` contain the off-diagonal elements of the bidiagonal matrix whose SVD is desired. On exit, E is overwritten.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: the algorithm failed = 1, a split was marked by a positive value in $E = 2$, current block of Z not diagonalized after $100 \, N$ iterations (in inner while loop)  On exit D and E represent a matrix with the same singular values which the calling subroutine could use to finish the computation, or even feed back into $\mathrm{DLASQ1} = 3$, termination criterion of outer while loop not met (program created more than N unreduced blocks)

</section>

-   `dlasq1()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLASQ1`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlasq1.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlasq1 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlasq1';

// Compute the singular values of an upper bidiagonal matrix with diagonal `d` and superdiagonal `e`:
const N = 4;
let d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0 ] );
let e = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.5, 0.25 ] );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 4 * N );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dlasq1( N, d, 1, e, 1, WORK );
console.log( info, d ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0 ] );
e = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.5, 0.25 ] );
info = dlasq1.ndarray( N, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, d ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLASQ1`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLASQ1 computes the singular values of a real N-by-N bidiagonal matrix with diagonal D and off-diagonal E. The singular values are computed to high relative accuracy, in the absence of denormalization, underflow and overflow. The algorithm was first presented in

"Accurate singular values and differential qd algorithms" by K. V. Fernando and B. N. Parlett, Numer. Math., Vol-67, No. 2, pp. 191-230, 1994,

and the present implementation is described in "An implementation of the dqds Algorithm (Positive Case)", LAPACK Working Note.

</section>
